slots.name: death toll
slots.sentence: A bad storm in early January caused flooding, ice storms and tornadoes across the eastern half of North America. The death toll was 56 across the U.S. and Canada. Hundreds of homes were destroyed, and millions were left without power.

slots.name: rain amount
slots.sentence: Florida was drenched in December, with Tampa receiving more than 15 inches of rain. In January, New Orleans received more than 19 inches, Mobile, Alabama, had 17 inches, and Asheville, North Carolina, had 10.

slots.name: cloud streak
slots.sentence: Des Moines, Iowa, had an 11-day cloud streak in December, the report said, and the normally sunny Albuquerque, New Mexico, saw no sun in the days leading up to Christmas.

slots.name: Lake Erie temperature
slots.sentence: By the end of February, Lake Erie at Buffalo was still unfrozen, with water temperature at 36 degrees.

slots.name: heating cost change
slots.sentence: One upside of the weird weather was that that heating costs were 10% lower nationwide when compared to a normal year.

events.label: April 1998 report on 1997-1998 El Niño winter

slots.name: start year
slots.sentence: Ehsan said in a September media briefing that this year’s atmospheric evolution looks similar to that of 1997, when one of the strongest-ever El Niños formed.

slots.name: end year
slots.sentence: That winter was characterized by broken records and “unusual extremes,” climate researchers said in an April 1998 National Climatic Data Center report.

slots.name: record start year
slots.sentence: It was the country’s second-warmest and seventh-wettest winter since 1895, and the super-strong El Niño contributed to chaotic weather from coast to coast.
